title: ASP.NET Over-Posting and Mass Assignment
platform_conditions: ASP.NET Core and ASP.NET (MVC/API) model binding; applies where request data is bound directly to domain objects
security_mechanism: The model binder enumerates every public settable property whose name matches a form-field, route, or query key and assigns the supplied value, regardless of what the UI sends. Binding directly to a domain/EF entity lets an attacker add isadmin=true or rowversion fields to an ordinary form post and promote or corrupt records; the same shape appears when a controller accepts the entity type and passes it straight to DbContext.Update. Authorization/antiforgery filters declared on a base class are silently not inherited when overridden, so a controller that re-declares its own attributes can drop protections without any diff at the action level.

source_sink_clues.source: Form bodies, query strings, route values, and JSON bodies whose keys the attacker chooses (the request itself).
source_sink_clues.sink: Action parameters bound directly to entity types ([FromForm] User entity, User entity) followed by DbContext.Add/Update or direct persistence; controller classes whose [Authorize]/[ValidateAntiForgeryToken] attributes are re-declared and thereby overridden

tracking_guards: Check the bound model is a narrow DTO containing only editable fields (plus [Bind] attribute inclusion lists on legacy MVC); check the service layer maps DTO to entity field-by-field; check that authorization and antiforgery attributes exist on the concrete controller/action actually reached, not only on a base class.
not_candidate_when: The action binds a DTO without sensitive setters, an explicit [Bind] include list excludes security-relevant properties, the service layer copies only whitelisted fields onto the persisted entity, or the field the attacker could set is recomputed server-side before saving.
public_references: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/915.html
